questionText: Design a URL shortener like bit.ly. Walk through your complete architecture.
idealAnswer: Core: encode long URL to 6-8 char short code (base62: 62^7 = 3.5T unique URLs). Storage: hash map in DB. Redirect: 301 (permanent, browser caches) vs 302 (temporary, tracks clicks). DB: key-value store (DynamoDB/Redis) for O(1) lookup. Scale reads with CDN. Collision: check existence + retry. Custom aliases: user-provided code. Analytics: async tracking via message queue. Rate limit creation per IP.
followUpHints: How do you prevent collision at scale?

questionText: Design a real-time chat system like WhatsApp. Support 1:1 and group messaging.
idealAnswer: WebSocket connections per user maintained to chat servers. Connection mapping: user → server in Redis. Message flow: sender → chat server → message DB (Cassandra — write-heavy, time-series) + recipient's server via service discovery. Offline: store undelivered messages, push notification. Group chat: fanout to all members. Message ordering: Snowflake IDs or per-conversation sequence. Read receipts: async. Media: S3 + CDN.

questionText: Design a distributed rate limiter that works across multiple servers.
idealAnswer: Centralized Redis for distributed counting. Sliding window with Redis sorted sets (timestamp as score, ZCOUNT for window). Issues: single Redis = SPOF → use Redis cluster. Lua scripts for atomicity. Local rate limiting as fast path. Response headers: X-RateLimit-Remaining. Soft vs hard limits. Rate limit by: IP, user ID, API key. Different limits per endpoint/tier. Graceful degradation when Redis is down.

questionText: Design a news feed system like Twitter/Facebook. Explain fanout strategies.
idealAnswer: Fanout-on-write (push): when user posts, pre-populate all followers' feeds. Fast reads, expensive writes for celebrities. Fanout-on-read (pull): compute feed at read time by merging followed users' posts. Flexible but slow for large follow graphs. Hybrid: fanout-on-write for regular users, fanout-on-read for celebrity accounts (>500K followers). Storage: Redis sorted set per user (postId as score=timestamp). Feed generation limit: top 500-1000 posts. Pagination: cursor-based.
followUpHints: How do you handle the celebrity problem?

questionText: Design a distributed cache like Redis or Memcached.
idealAnswer: Consistent hashing maps keys to nodes — adding/removing node only moves ~1/n keys. Each node stores key-value with TTL. Replication: primary-replica for availability. Eviction: LRU (most common). Cache coherence: write-through or invalidation on update. Client-side sharding vs proxy-based (Redis Cluster). Hot keys: replicate popular keys across multiple shards. Memory management: slab allocation (Memcached).

questionText: Design a search autocomplete system (typeahead) that returns suggestions as users type.
idealAnswer: Trie data structure for prefix matching. Scale: distribute Trie across servers by prefix range. Ranking: store top-k results at each Trie node (updated async via aggregation pipeline). Data collection: log search queries, aggregate in Hadoop/Spark, update Trie periodically. Caching: Redis for popular prefixes (high hit rate). Response time: <100ms requirement. Personalization: blend global suggestions with user history.

questionText: Design a video streaming service like YouTube. Focus on upload, storage, and playback.
idealAnswer: Upload: direct to S3 via presigned URL. Processing: async transcoding pipeline (FFmpeg) to multiple resolutions/codecs (H.264, VP9). Message queue triggers transcoding workers. Storage: S3 + CDN (CloudFront). Adaptive bitrate streaming (ABR): HLS or DASH — video split into 2-10 second chunks, client selects quality based on bandwidth. Metadata: MySQL for video info. Search: Elasticsearch. Thumbnail: extracted from first few frames.

questionText: Design a push notification system that supports iOS, Android, and email at scale.
idealAnswer: Notification service receives events and routes based on user preferences and device type. iOS: APNs (Apple Push Notification). Android: FCM (Firebase). Email: SendGrid/SES. Architecture: event → notification service → queue per channel → channel workers → provider. Worker pattern enables retry with exponential backoff. Deduplication: idempotency key prevents duplicate sends. User preferences DB determines channel priority. Bulk notifications: fan-out via partitioned queues.

questionText: What is an API gateway? Design one with rate limiting, auth, and routing.
idealAnswer: API gateway is the single entry point for all clients. Responsibilities: authentication (verify JWT/API key), authorization, rate limiting, request routing to microservices, SSL termination, request/response transformation, logging/tracing, caching. Routing: path-based (/users → user service, /orders → order service). Load balancing per service. Circuit breaker for failing services. Kong, AWS API Gateway, nginx. Plugin architecture for extensibility.

questionText: Design a distributed file storage system like Google Drive or Dropbox.
idealAnswer: Client sync: delta encoding, only upload changed blocks (chunking files into 4MB blocks). Chunked upload: parallel + resumable. Storage: Google Cloud Storage/S3 for raw data. Metadata DB: file tree, version history (MySQL + change log). Conflict resolution: last-write-wins or merge. Deduplication: content-addressable storage (hash of file = storage key). Sharing: access control lists (ACLs). CDN for popular files. Mobile sync: careful battery/bandwidth management.

questionText: Design the backend for a ride-sharing app like Uber. Focus on matching and location tracking.
idealAnswer: Location updates: drivers send GPS every 4 seconds via WebSocket. Storage: Redis geospatial (GEOADD, GEORADIUS) for real-time driver positions. Matching: GEORADIUS query to find nearby drivers, rank by ETA (Google Maps API). Trip lifecycle: requested → matched → en-route → arrived → completed. Dispatch service: assigns driver. Surge pricing: demand/supply ratio in geohash cells. Payments: async via queue. Trip history: PostgreSQL.

questionText: Design a web crawler and search engine. What's the architecture for indexing and ranking?
idealAnswer: Crawler: seed URLs → BFS queue → fetch → parse links + extract text → store. Politeness: robots.txt, crawl delay per domain. Deduplication: URL normalization + hash set. Index: inverted index (term → document list with positions). Storage: distributed (each shard handles part of index). Ranking: TF-IDF for relevance + PageRank for authority. Serving: query parsing → index lookup → ranking → snippet extraction. Real-time updates vs batch index builds.

questionText: Design a real-time collaborative document editor like Google Docs.
idealAnswer: Approach 1: Operational Transform (OT) — transform concurrent operations to preserve intent. Complex to implement correctly. Approach 2: CRDTs (Conflict-free Replicated Data Types) — mathematical data structures that merge automatically. Yjs, Automerge. WebSocket for real-time sync. Each client gets same document after convergence. History: append-only log of operations. Awareness: cursor positions, user presence. Snapshots + operation logs for efficient startup (don't replay all history).
followUpHints: Offline editing with sync on reconnect

questionText: Design a recommendation system (e.g., Netflix, Spotify). What algorithms and data pipelines are involved?
idealAnswer: Collaborative filtering: find users with similar taste, recommend what they liked. Problem: cold start for new users. Content-based: recommend similar items based on features. Matrix factorization (Singular Value Decomposition): decompose user-item rating matrix to find latent factors — scales better. Pipelines: offline training (Spark) on historical interaction data → model stored in feature store → real-time serving. A/B test different algorithms. Two-stage: candidate generation → ranking. Embeddings for item/user representations.
followUpHints: How do you solve cold start?

questionText: Design a distributed cron job scheduler that supports millions of jobs.
idealAnswer: Job storage: DB with next_run_at timestamp. Polling workers: scan for due jobs, acquire distributed lock (Redis Redlock or DB row lock) to prevent double execution. Partitioning: divide jobs by hash of job_id across worker pools. Leader election for coordination. Retry with exponential backoff + dead letter queue. Job types: one-time vs recurring (cron expression parsing). Missed runs: configurable catch-up or skip. Monitoring: job execution history, failed job alerts.
followUpHints: How to handle job failures across regions?

questionText: Design an inventory management system that prevents overselling when flash sales happen.
idealAnswer: Prevent overselling: optimistic locking (version field + WHERE version=x in UPDATE) or pessimistic locking (SELECT FOR UPDATE). For high concurrency flash sales: Redis atomic DECR on inventory counter (prevents race conditions), persist to DB async. Queue incoming orders during peak. Reserve inventory on cart add, release on timeout. DB constraint: inventory >= 0. Rollback on payment failure releases reserved stock.

questionText: Design a payment processing system. How do you ensure exactly-once payment processing?
idealAnswer: Idempotency keys: client generates UUID per payment, server deduplicates. Store idempotency key + result. Two-phase: create payment intent → execute. Saga pattern for multi-step (reserve funds → process → settle). Async: queue-based processing with acknowledgment. Reconciliation: daily batch compare transactions with bank statements. Ledger: double-entry accounting (debit one account, credit another). PCI compliance: never store raw card numbers (tokenize with Stripe/Braintree). Retry with exponential backoff.

questionText: Design an ad click tracking system that handles 10,000 clicks/second with real-time analytics.
idealAnswer: Click event → Kafka (buffer, decouple) → stream processor (Flink/Spark Streaming) → real-time aggregation (counts per ad, per hour) stored in Redis → periodic flush to data warehouse (Redshift/BigQuery) for historical analytics. Click deduplication: Redis Bloom filter to detect bot/duplicate clicks. Impression vs click vs conversion funnel. Batch aggregation for billing reports. Latency: click acknowledgment must be fast (<100ms) — async everything after receipt.

questionText: Design a proximity search feature (like 'find restaurants near me') that works at global scale.
idealAnswer: Geospatial indexing strategies: Geohash (encode location as prefix string, nearby cells share prefix — PostgreSQL, Redis GEOADD), Quadtree (recursive 2D space partitioning), H3 (Uber — hexagonal grid). Two-step: geohash cell → expand if not enough results. Static POIs: DB + geospatial index. Dynamic (moving objects): Redis GEOADD/GEORADIUS. Caching: tile-based (precompute results per geohash level). CDN for static map tiles.
followUpHints: How to handle moving objects efficiently?

questionText: How would you handle distributed transactions across multiple microservices without two-phase commit?
idealAnswer: 2PC problems: blocking protocol, coordinator SPOF, poor availability. Saga pattern: long-lived transaction broken into local transactions with compensating actions on failure. Choreography saga: services emit events, each reacts and emits next. Orchestration saga: central coordinator (saga orchestrator) calls services sequentially. Outbox pattern: write event to same DB as domain data in single transaction, then async publish to event bus — solves dual-write. Eventual consistency is the trade-off. Idempotent consumers ensure safe retry.
